healthInfo.healthcareSystem: Mixed public/private. Public healthcare (State hospitals) is available but often overcrowded with long wait times. Private healthcare (medical schemes) offers excellent care comparable to first-world standards.
healthInfo.qualityNotes: Private healthcare in South Africa is excellent and world-class, with JCI-accredited hospitals in major cities. State hospitals are basic and overcrowded. Medical staff are well-trained. Pharmacies (Clicks, Dis-Chem, independent) are widely available. Private ambulance services (ER24, Netcare 911) are excellent but expensive.
healthInfo.pharmacyHours: Most pharmacies open 8am-9pm; some 24-hour pharmacies in major cities; chains include Clicks, Dis-Chem Pharmacies, and independent pharmacies
healthInfo.pharmacyTips: Many common medications available OTC. Pharmacists are helpful and knowledgeable. Bring a list of medications with generic names. Some medications may not be available — bring your supply. Malaria prophylaxis is important for certain regions.
healthInfo.prescriptionRules: A prescription is required for prescription medications. Foreign prescriptions are not accepted — you need a South African prescription. Carry all medications in original packaging with a doctor's note.

restrictedMeds.name: ADHD stimulant medications (Adderall, Ritalin, Vyvanse)
restrictedMeds.note: Stimulants are Schedule 6 controlled substances. Bring original prescription, doctor's letter, and only the amount needed. You may need a permit from the South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA) for certain quantities.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Codeine is a Schedule 5/6 substance. Some products available with prescription. Many codeine products require a prescription. Carry alternatives if possible.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications (diazepam, alprazolam, etc.)
restrictedMeds.note: Benzodiazepines are controlled. Carry a doctor's letter explaining medical necessity.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis (medical or recreational)
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis is illegal in South Africa despite some decriminalization for personal use. Do not bring any cannabis products.

restrictedMeds.name: Methylphenidate (Ritalin/Concerta)
restrictedMeds.note: Schedule 6 controlled. Bring documentation and SAHPRA permit if carrying significant quantities.

healthInfo.bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. For controlled substances, carry original prescriptions and a note explaining medical necessity. Check SAHPRA requirements if carrying Schedule 5-6 substances for extended stays.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Required for visa applications but not for entry. Strongly recommended for all travelers. Medical care without insurance in private hospitals can be expensive ($1,000-5,000+/day).
travelInsurance.tips: Travel insurance is strongly recommended. State hospitals are free but overcrowded. Private healthcare is excellent but expensive without insurance. Medical evacuation coverage is essential, especially for safari ( Kruger) and remote areas. Crime-related injuries are also a risk — ensure coverage includes trauma and emergency medical services.

recommended: Typhoid (for extended stays or rural travel)
Yellow Fever (required if arriving from a yellow fever endemic country)
Rabies (for animal exposure, especially dogs and wildlife)
Malaria prophylaxis (for travel to Kruger National Park and surrounding areas, and KwaZulu-Natal lowlands during summer months)
vaccinations.notes: No required vaccinations for most travelers unless arriving from a yellow fever endemic country. Malaria is a risk in Kruger National Park and some coastal areas — take prophylaxis (Larium/mefloquine, Malarone, or doxycycline). Rabies is present in some areas — avoid contact with dogs and wild animals.

healthInfo.waterNotes: Tap water is generally safe to drink in major cities (Johannesburg, Cape Town, Durban). In rural areas, use bottled or filtered water as a precaution. In Cape Town, tap water is excellent. Bottled water is widely available everywhere.
healthInfo.foodSafetyTips: South Africa has good food safety standards in restaurants, hotels, and supermarkets. In Cape Town and major cities, restaurants maintain excellent hygiene. Be cautious with street food in informal areas. South African wine country and safari lodges maintain high standards. Avoid meat from informal vendors.
healthInfo.medicalTourismNote: South Africa is a well-established medical tourism destination, particularly for cosmetic surgery, cardiac surgery, and fertility treatments. Costs are 50-80% lower than in the US and UK. Cape Town and Johannesburg have world-class JCI-accredited private hospitals. Popular for tummy tucks, breast augmentations, and cardiac procedures.
